question_text: Wisdom lies in knowing what to reckon with and what to overlook. An officer being engrossed with the periphery, ignoring the core issues before him, is not rare in the bureaucracy. Do you agree that such preoccupation of an administrator leads to travesty of justice to the cause of effective service delivery and good governance? Critically evaluate. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: Wisdom here is a choice of what deserves the file
A busy officer can still be unjust if the busyness is peripheral
Not every small matter is peripheral; a citizen's delay can be the core
The agreement is qualified: preoccupation misleads when it replaces the mandate

points.text: Yes, with a qualification. An officer lost in the margin can fail the very people the office exists for.
Effective delivery needs a ranking: the entitlement, the safety and the decision that only this officer can take come first.
A meeting, a protocol and a peripheral complaint feel like work and produce no service.
The qualification is that some 'small' files are the core for a poor applicant. Overlooking those is the same travesty.
The preoccupation is a failure of justice when it is an escape from the decision the post was made to take.

question_text: Apart from intellectual competency and moral qualities, empathy and compassion are some of the other vital attributes that facilitate the civil servants to be more competent in tackling the crucial issues or taking critical decisions. Explain with suitable illustrations. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: Competence is not only a correct rule
Empathy reads the person the rule will land on
Compassion moves the officer to reduce avoidable harm
Neither replaces the rule; both stop a lawful cruelty

points.text: Empathy and compassion make a competent decision because a crucial issue is never only technical.
Empathy is understanding the applicant's constraint: a migrant who cannot return for a second hearing, a widow who cannot read the form.
Compassion is then acting to reduce that harm within the law — a camp hearing, a help desk, a benefit that is not delayed for a missing photocopy.
Without them an officer can be clever and still take a decision the field will not survive.
They do not soften a duty. They tell the officer whom the duty is for.

question_text: The Rules and Regulations provided to all the civil servants are same, yet there is difference in the performance. Positive minded officers are able to interpret the Rules and Regulations in favour of the case and achieve success, whereas negative minded officers are unable to achieve goals by interpreting the same Rules and Regulations against the case. Discuss with illustrations. (Answer in 150 words)
topic: Attitude and the reading of rules
topics: Attitude and the reading of rules
subTopics: Positive and negative reading of rules
keyPointers: The same rule can be read as a path or as a wall
A positive mind looks for the lawful way to the public purpose
A negative mind looks for the clause that stops the file
Attitude changes performance only inside the rule, not by breaking it

points.text: The difference in performance often lies in the attitude brought to an identical rule.
A positive officer reads a discretion in favour of a genuine beneficiary and finds the enabling clause.
A negative officer reads every discretion as a risk and returns the file.
The illustration is a relief payment: one officer uses the permitted relaxation for a disaster; the other cites the missing document and waits.
The limit is that 'in favour of the case' must still be lawful. A positive mind is not a licence.
Attitude decides whether the rule is used to deliver or to delay.

question_text: It is believed that adherence to ethics in human actions would ensure in smooth functioning of an organization/system. If so, what does ethics seek to promote in human life? How do ethical values assist in the resolution of conflicts faced by him in his day-to-day functioning? (Answer in 150 words)
topic: What ethics promotes, and how it settles a conflict
topics: What ethics promotes, and how it settles a conflict
keyPointers: Ethics seeks a life that can be justified to others
It promotes trust, fairness and a limit on the self
A daily conflict is easier when a value has already ranked the claims
Smooth functioning follows because people can predict a fair colleague

points.text: Ethics seeks to promote a life in which one's actions can be defended as fair to those affected.
That includes honesty, a respect for persons, and the habit of not taking an unfair advantage.
In a daily conflict — a target against a truth, a friend's request against a rule — a prior value tells which claim yields.
The resolution is then explainable, so the loser of the decision can still trust the system.
An organisation runs smoothly when that predictability replaces fear and favour.

question_text: What does this quotation mean to you? “Ethics is knowing the difference between what you have the right to do and what is right to do.” — Potter Stewart (Answer in 150 words)
topic: Potter Stewart on right and rightful
topics: Potter Stewart on right and rightful
keyPointers: A right is a permission; the right thing is a judgement
Power and legality can both be misused without breaking a rule
The quote asks the officer to add a second question
Ethics begins where the law stops instructing

points.text: Stewart separates what one may do from what one should do.
A legal power — to transfer, to delay, to stay silent — can be exercised in a way that is permitted and still wrong.
The difference is the harm to a person who cannot answer back.
For a public servant the quote means: do not stop at 'am I allowed'. Ask 'is this the use the power was given for'.
Ethics is that second question.

question_text: What does this quotation mean to you? “If a country is to be corruption free and become a nation of beautiful minds, I strongly feel that there are three key societal members who can make a difference. They are father, mother and teacher.” — A. P. J. Abdul Kalam (Answer in 150 words)
topic: Kalam on parents, teachers and corruption
topics: Kalam on parents, teachers and corruption
keyPointers: Kalam locates a clean public life in the first teachers
A father, a mother and a teacher set what a child treats as normal
A law catches a corrupt act; these three prevent the willingness
Beautiful minds are honest minds, not only clever ones

points.text: Kalam means that a corruption-free country is raised before it is policed.
The parent who does not boast of a bribe, and the teacher who will not sell a mark, teach that a shortcut is shameful.
A child who never sees that lesson meets the state later as a customer of favours.
The quote does not excuse the law. It says the law arrives too late if the home and the school have already licensed the act.
The three are key because they form the person the institution later employs.

question_text: What does this quotation mean to you? “Judge your success by what you had to give up in order to get it.” — Dalai Lama (Answer in 150 words)
topic: Dalai Lama on the cost of success
topics: Dalai Lama on the cost of success
keyPointers: Success has a price that the prize itself hides
What was given up may be integrity, health, a relationship or a duty
A gain that costs a value is a failure on a longer account
The quote is a test, not a call to give up ambition

points.text: The Dalai Lama asks that success be weighed by its sacrifice, not by its shine.
A promotion got by silence at a wrong, or a profit got by a worker's health, fails this test.
A success that cost comfort, or a lazy habit, can pass it.
For public life the quote means: look at the value that was spent, and decide if the post was worth that value.
The measure of success is the person who remains after it.

question_text: What do you understand by the term 'good governance'? How far recent initiatives in terms of e-Governance steps taken by the State have helped the beneficiaries? Discuss with suitable examples. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: Good governance is a service that is lawful, quick and answerable
E-governance helps where it removes a queue and a discretion
It helps less where the user cannot reach the screen
The test is the beneficiary, not the portal

points.text: Good governance is public power used in a way that is transparent, accountable, and actually delivered.
E-governance has helped: a direct transfer, an online certificate, a public dashboard and a grievance with a number reduce the tout.
Examples such as a digital public payment and an online land or passport service show the gain.
The help stops at the person without a device, a document or a language the portal uses. A camp and an assisted access are part of the same reform.
The initiatives have helped a great deal, and only as far as the last beneficiary can use them.

question_text: Online methodology is being used for day-to-day meetings, institutional approvals in the administration and for teaching and learning in education sector to the extent telemedicine in the health sector is getting popular with the approvals of the competent authority. No doubt, it has advantages and disadvantages for both the beneficiaries and the system at large. Describe and discuss the ethical issues involved in the use of online method particularly to the vulnerable section of the society. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: Online delivery can include and can abandon in the same click
Consent, privacy and a real access are the ethical issues
The vulnerable pay the exclusion and also the data risk
Convenience for the system is not automatically fairness

points.text: The ethical issue is that an online method treats unequally people who are unequal in access.
A patient, a student or an applicant without a device, a language or a quiet room is silently dropped.
Telemedicine and online teaching also raise consent and the privacy of a health or a child's data.
A hurried approval on a screen can skip the hearing a vulnerable person needed.
The ethical duty is an assisted option, a human appeal, and a data use that the person could have refused.
Online is ethical only when the person who cannot log in is still served.

question_text: Russia and Ukraine war has been going on for the last seven months. Different countries have taken independent stands and actions keeping in view their own national interests. We are all aware that war has its own impact on the different aspects of society, including human tragedy. What are those ethical issues that are crucial to be considered while launching the war and its continuation so far? Illustrate with justification the ethical issues involved in the given state of affair. (Answer in 150 words)
topic: Ethical issues in launching and continuing a war
topics: Ethical issues in launching and continuing a war
keyPointers: Launching a war needs a justification heavier than an interest
Continuation needs a fresh look at the human cost already paid
National interest does not erase the duty to civilians and to proportion
The bystander state's interest is also an ethical fact, not only a strategy

points.text: The ethical issues are whether force was justified, whether it stays proportionate, and who bears a cost they did not choose.
A decision to launch must meet a just cause, a right authority and a last resort. An interest in territory or status is not enough.
Continuation after mass civilian death has to be re-justified, not assumed.
Other countries' 'independent stands' raise a further issue: energy, grain and a refugee are moral facts, and a neutrality that feeds the war is not morally empty.
The crucial issue is that a national interest is being purchased with lives that are not the decision-maker's.

question_text: Write short notes on the following in 30 words each: (i) Constitutional morality (ii) Conflict of interest (iii) Probity in public life (iv) Challenges of digitalization (v) Devotion to duty
topic: Five short ideas in public ethics
topics: Five short ideas in public ethics
keyPointers: Constitutional morality is loyalty to the Constitution's ethic, not only to its text
A conflict of interest is a private stake in a public decision
Probity is honesty that can be seen
Digitalisation's challenge is exclusion and a data misuse
Devotion to duty is staying with the task when it is dull or costly

points.text: These five terms are working tests of a public life.
Constitutional morality: following the spirit of equality, liberty and the restraint the Constitution expects, even when a shortcut is popular.
Conflict of interest: a personal gain, a relative or a future job that could bend the decision. The remedy is disclosure and recusal.
Probity: conduct whose honesty does not depend on not being caught.
Digitalisation: reaching the person without a device, and not turning a service into a surveillance.
Devotion to duty: completing the assigned public task with care, including the part nobody will applaud.
Together they describe an officer who is constitutional, unbought, careful with a new tool, and still at the desk.

question_text: Whistle-blower, who reports corruption and illegal activities, wrongdoing and misconduct to the concerned authorities, runs the risk of being exposed to grave danger, physical harm and victimization by the vested interests, accused persons and his team. What policy measures would you suggest to strengthen protection mechanism to safeguard the whistle-blower? (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: A report of corruption is a public good and a personal risk
Protection has to cover identity, the body and the job
A law that punishes the act and does not shield the reporter will not be used
The mechanism must be independent of the accused's department

points.text: Protect the person, or the information will stop coming.
A confidential identity, a route that does not pass through the accused, and a quick physical protection where there is a threat.
A bar on transfer, suspension or a false case as revenge, with a penalty for victimisation.
A reward is secondary. Safety and reinstatement are the policy.
An independent authority, not the same office, must receive the report and watch the retaliation.
The measure that matters is that a truthful reporter is safer after speaking than before.

question_text: In contemporary world, corporate sector's contribution in generating wealth and employment is increasing. In doing so, they are bringing in unprecedented onslaught on the climate, environmental sustainability and living conditions of human beings. In this background, do you find that Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is efficient and sufficient enough to fulfill the social roles and responsibilities needed in the corporate world for which the CSR is mandated? Critically examine. (Answer in 150 words)
keyPointers: CSR spends a slice of profit on a social good
The harm in the question is caused by the main business, not by the missing donation
CSR can be efficient at projects and still be insufficient
The duty required is in how the profit is made

points.text: CSR is a useful instrument and an insufficient answer.
A mandated spend can build a school or a water project, and some firms do this well.
It does not, by its design, stop the emission, the effluent or the labour condition that created the profit.
A company can meet the CSR number and miss the responsibility.
Sufficiency would require the duty to sit inside the business: a limit, a liability and a disclosure, with CSR as a supplement.
CSR is not enough for the social role the question describes.

question_text: Prabhat, Vice President (Marketing) at Sterling Electric Ltd., is under pressure as sales fall and his division may be closed. He is the sole earner for two children and an ailing mother, with a home-loan EMI. A candidate, Subhash Verma, whose CV came through the Defence Minister's office, offers copies of a rival's bid for a secret defence tender near Gwalior, if Sterling employs him. Accepting would likely win the tender. (a) Discuss the ethical issues. (b) Critically examine Prabhat's options. (c) Which option is most appropriate, and why? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: A stolen rival bid and a job offer
topics: A stolen rival bid and a job offer
keyPointers: The documents are not his to use
A private distress does not license a corrupt tender
Hiring on merit is separate from buying a theft
The appropriate option refuses the papers and reports the offer

points.text: Ethical issues: theft of a competitor's bid, a compromised defence tender, a CV routed through a minister's office, and a man using his family's need to justify the wrong.

Options: accept and win; refuse quietly and hire Verma on merit if he truly is best; refuse, record the offer and inform the company and, because a defence tender is involved, the proper authority; or stall.
Accepting is a short win and a crime. Quiet refusal leaves the next officer exposed. Stalling is only delay.

The appropriate option is to refuse the documents, not to trade a job for them, to put the offer on record, and to let the tender proceed honestly. His personal loan is real and is not a reason to steal a bid.

question_text: Ramesh, a State civil servant newly posted as Director in the Home Department of a border State, catches security staff colluding in the infiltration of illegal migrants, who are then given forged Aadhaar, ration and voter cards. His mother is in a cancer hospital in the capital and his children are in school there. After he submits a report, the Additional Home Secretary orders him to withdraw it, warning of a transfer and a blocked promotion. (a) What options does Ramesh have? (b) Which should he adopt, and why? (c) Critically evaluate each option. (d) What ethical dilemmas does he face? (e) What policy measures would you suggest against such infiltration? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: A border report and a threat to withdraw it
topics: A border report and a threat to withdraw it
keyPointers: Withdrawing a true report is a falsehood in the file
The family's dependence is the pressure, not the justification
The right option keeps the report and protects the family by lawful means
Infiltration needs a document trail, not only a brave officer

points.text: Options: withdraw the report; refuse and wait to be transferred; leak it; or refuse in writing, send the report to a lawful oversight, and ask for protection of the posting's substance rather than of his comfort.
Withdrawal saves the promotion and buries a crime. A leak can be true and still be the wrong channel. Silent refusal without a record is easily buried.
He should adopt the written refusal. The dilemma is his mother's treatment and his children's school against the duty he has already documented.
Policy: biometric and document verification at the border, rotation of the colluding posts, a fast check of forged cards, and a protection for the officer who reports.

question_text: Despite a Supreme Court ban, stone mining continues in a border district of the Aravallis with the connivance of forest officials and politicians. A young SP is killed when he tries to stop a loaded truck. Investigative journalist Ashok traces the nexus to the local MLA, who is close to the Chief Minister and is also a relative and an unofficial partner of the TV channel's owner. The CMD tells Ashok to drop the story and offers a promotion, a pay hike and adjustment of a ₹10 lakh loan taken for his son's treatment. (a) What options does Ashok have? (b) Critically evaluate each. (c) What ethical dilemmas does he face? (d) Which option is most appropriate, and why? (e) What training would you suggest for police posted to such districts? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: A buried mining story and a journalist's loan
topics: A buried mining story and a journalist's loan
keyPointers: The story is evidence of a death and a banned mining
The owner's interest is the conflict, not a reason to spike it
The child's treatment is the leverage, and it can be met without selling the report
The appropriate option keeps the facts in a channel the owner does not control

points.text: Options: hand over the report and take the relief; drop it quietly; run it on this channel against the order; or keep a copy, refuse the bargain, and offer the verified story to an independent outlet or a lawful authority.
Taking the bargain buries a killing. Running it only inside a captured channel will be killed in edit. Dropping it is the same result without the money.
The dilemma is his son's loan against the dead officer and the Court's ban.

The appropriate option is to refuse, preserve the evidence, and publish or file it where the MLA's share cannot stop it. Training for such districts: law on the mining ban, scene evidence, and how to report a nexus without a lone fatal chase.

question_text: You inspect final products at a shoe company that employs you, the sole support of aged parents, soon after your marriage. A large export consignment was rejected in Europe for poor quality. Top management orders it cleared for the domestic market. You report the defects; every other team member signs. You are told that if you do not clear it, your services will be terminated. (a) What options do you have? (b) Critically evaluate each. (c) Which would you adopt, and why? (d) What ethical dilemmas do you face? (e) What can follow from overlooking the inspection? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: A rejected export cleared for the home market
topics: A rejected export cleared for the home market
subTopics: Consumer safety against a threat of dismissal
keyPointers: A known defect does not become acceptable because the buyer is Indian
Signing is a personal certification, not a team courtesy
The job and the parents are the pressure
The right option is a written refusal and a record

points.text: Options: sign; refuse and resign; refuse in writing and escalate to the board or a consumer/standards authority if the defect is unsafe; or delay.
Signing protects the salary and cheats the domestic buyer. Resigning is clean and leaves the consignment cleared by others. Delay only helps the management.
The dilemma is parents and a new marriage against a certificate you know is false.

Adopt the written refusal. If the defect can harm a wearer, copy the finding to a lawful standard body. Overlooking it means injury, a lost brand, and a habit that the next export will also be lied about.

question_text: Rakesh, Joint Commissioner in a city's transport department, faces a drivers' strike. A bus driver died after a fight he started with a car driver; police found the bus driver used physical violence. Management wants to deny the family the extra compensation given to others who die on duty, and will not offer a job to a family member. The dead driver, 52, was the sole earner for a wife and two daughters. The strike is ten days old. (a) What options does Rakesh have? (b) Critically examine each. (c) What ethical dilemmas does he face? (d) What course of action should he take to diffuse the situation? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: A strike over compensation after a driver's fault
topics: A strike over compensation after a driver's fault
subTopics: Compassion and equal rules in a labour dispute
keyPointers: The death on duty and the driver's fault are both facts
A family should not be punished twice, nor should violence be rewarded as heroism
An open-ended strike punishes the public
The way out is a lawful compassion that does not erase the finding

points.text: Options: reject every demand; grant the full extra compensation and a job; break the strike by force; or separate the issues.

A total rejection ignores a widow and two students and prolongs the strike. A full reward equates a fight the driver started with a death in the course of driving. Force without an offer deepens the anger.
The dilemma is equal treatment of other dead drivers against not honouring an assault, and the public's buses against the family's hunger.

He should keep the service running by talking, pay the statutory and humanitarian support the family is due, refuse to treat the assault as an extra badge of honour, and offer a fair, rule-based consideration of employment rather than a forced post. Record the police finding so the distinction is principled.

question_text: You head a section in the Environment Pollution Control Board. Many small and medium units employ migrant workers but pollute air, water and soil despite holding clearance. Local people face persistent illness. You issue notices for fresh clearance. Owners, some politicians and workers turn hostile, fearing closure and unemployment. You receive threats, and also support from colleagues and local NGOs who want polluting units shut at once. (a) What options do you have? (b) Critically examine them. (c) What mechanism would you suggest to ensure compliance? (d) What ethical dilemmas did you face? (Answer in 250 words)
topic: Pollution notices against jobs and threats
topics: Pollution notices against jobs and threats
keyPointers: The illness is real and so is the migrant's wage
A notice that only closes units can be lawfully right and socially crude
Immediate total closure and looking away are both failures
The mechanism is a timed compliance, not a single dramatic order

points.text: Options: withdraw the notices; shut every unit at once; or keep the notice and run a time-bound compliance with an inspection the public can see.
Withdrawal abandons the sick. Instant closure throws migrant workers out and invites a political reversal. A vague notice with no help will be fought and then ignored.
The dilemma is health against a livelihood, and your own safety against the duty.

Suggest a mechanism: published standards, a short deadline to install treatment, independent sampling, a penalty that rises, closure only for the unit that will not comply, and a labour help for workers of a unit that must shut. Record the threats. Do not trade the notice for peace.
